scientific_question: Can a deformable physical twin continuously monitor a shadow learned correction, authorize it at an optional stopping time under delayed outcomes, and retain a bounded lifetime false-promotion budget across externally restarted epochs?

null_calibration.purpose: implementation calibration only; the mathematical guarantee is supplied by the e-process construction and Ville's inequality

theorem_contract.gain_null: For every revealed trial i, E[X_i | F_{i-1}] <= 0 for the registered bounded gain score X_i in [-1,1].
theorem_contract.harm_null: For every revealed trial i, P(H_i=1 | F_{i-1}) >= q for the registered harm event and ceiling q.
theorem_contract.predictability: Candidate, fallback, trial inclusion, cap, margin, bet mixtures, epoch index, and reveal order are fixed or predictable before the corresponding target loss is revealed.
theorem_contract.epoch_statement: For either null, the probability of any threshold crossing over an unbounded externally restarted epoch sequence is at most the corresponding total alpha budget.
theorem_contract.combined_statement: If at least one registered null holds in every active epoch, but the active null may differ between epochs, a union bound gives a lifetime false-authorization probability no larger than total_alpha_gain plus total_alpha_harm, here 0.05. If one fixed null holds throughout all epochs, its corresponding 0.025 budget applies.
theorem_contract.multiple_candidates: A family of correction candidates requires a separate preregistered alpha allocation or an e-value merger; this protocol evaluates one fixed candidate.

claim_boundary: A passing result supports a controlled mechanism claim that the registered e-process admission rule can authorize a beneficial shadow correction under delayed feedback while empirical null simulations remain below the alpha-spent false-promotion budget. The theorem remains conditional on the registered bounded scores, predictable information order, and conditional nulls. It does not establish real-object performance, arbitrary nonstationarity, universal safety, or state of the art.
